subject: general
question: A pipe can fill a tank in 8 hours. Another pipe can empty the filled tank in 72 hours. If both the pipes are opened simultaneously, then the time (in hours) in which the tank will be one-third filled, is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net efficiency = **Efficiency of Filling Pipe − Efficiency of Emptying Pipe**.

Total Capacity (LCM of 8, 72) = **72 units**.

Filling efficiency = 9, Emptying efficiency = 1 → Combined efficiency = **8 units/hr**.

Time for 1/3rd tank = (72 ÷ 3) ÷ 8 = **24 ÷ 8 = 3 hours**.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Filling time = 8 hours, Emptying time = 72 hours.

**Formula:** Total Work = LCM of times; Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time.

 **Pipe**
 **Time (hrs)**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**

 Filling Pipe (A)
 8
 72
 +9

 Emptying Pipe (B)
 72
 −1

⇒ Combined Efficiency of (A + B) = 9 − 1 = **8 units/hr**

⇒ Required capacity to fill = 1/3 × 72 = **24 units**

⇒ Time required = 24 ÷ 8 = **3 hours**

**∴ The correct answer is 3 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

Inlet pipes add water (positive efficiency) while outlet/leakage pipes remove water (negative efficiency).

Combined Rate Formula

If pipe A fills in 'x' hours and pipe B empties in 'y' hours, net rate per hour = (1/x − 1/y).

Time and Work Relation

Time taken to complete a specific fraction of work = (Fraction × Total Work) ÷ Combined Efficiency.</p
